label: PF Backlog 585
title: EDP-04: Data-plane threat model + data-flow register (cross-tenant IDOR, path traversal, token/role spoofing, object-URL leakage, egress, residency bypass)
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.

brief.problem: Data plane has no documented threat model or data-flow inventory.
brief.what_adds: Versioned data-flow register + threat model with Go validation.
brief.why: Downstream EDP policy work needs a canonical threat inventory.

objective: Produce an EDP-04 data-plane threat model and versioned data-flow register covering IDOR, path traversal, token/role spoofing, object-URL leakage, egress, and residency bypass.
acceptance_criteria: Data-flow register covers all 6 threat categories with source/sink mapping
Findings link to ADR decisions from BI-PF-1293
approach: Register-first: enumerate flows, map threats, encode checks in Go.
risks: Threat model could go stale without CI enforcement
rollback: Revert new register/config and docs; no runtime impact.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Author a Go data-flow register + threat model doc as config-driven register (extend config/compliance-register.json pattern) with a small Go validator package; consume ADR decisions from BI-PF-1293.
dependency_findings: RELATED BI-PF-1297 consumes data-flow register as policy input
conflict_findings: Low: touches config/ + new docs only; no overlap with EDP-11/14 code
duplication_findings: No existing threat-model register in components; compliance-register.json closest pattern
BI-PF-1298 perf capture shares data-flow inventory but scoped to metrics, not threats
analysis.rationale: Doc+register deliverable with new validator component; no equivalent work exists in backlog.
risks: Threat model could go stale without CI enforcement
missing_info: Register format (JSON vs YAML) and owning security reviewer
Scope of egress/residency rules beyond BI-PF-1297

consolidation_proposal.title: EDP-04: Data-plane threat model + data-flow register (cross-tenant IDOR, path traversal, token/role spoofing, object-URL leakage, egress, residency bypass)
consolidation_proposal.body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-1292. Source: docs/Product_Forge_Enterprise_Performance_Security_DB_Storage_Roadmap.md. Phase item (see epic). Language rule L1 = Go; must pass scripts/dev/language_rule_review.py.
acceptance_criteria: Threat model enumerates cross-tenant IDOR, traversal/symlink, token/role spoofing, object-URL leakage, noisy-neighbor, compromised worker, backup exposure, tenant deletion, cross-region/egress and residency-bypass.
Each threat maps to an owner interface/control and a test.
Data-flow register covers all copies (versions, WAL, replicas, caches, queues, logs, exports, model calls).
ADR document committed covering storage layers, backends, and data-flow decisions
Develop commit SHA pinned and recorded
The 11 interfaces are declared with explicit optional capabilities (versioning/lock/conditional-write/KMS/signed-URL/multipart).
A conformance suite runs against any adapter (starting with WorkerGrid's store as reference).
No domain module depends on a concrete provider.
tenant.home_region, jurisdiction_profile_id, residency_policy_version are set at provisioning from authenticated config (never from X-Tenant-Id/X-Region/URL).
Provisioning fails closed if any required service (DB/object/backup/logs/KMS/queue/cache/vector/workers/model) lacks an approved region.
Region is immutable to ordinary users; changes require an audited migration plan.

context_review.reason: Format and reviewer are human decisions; threat categories and ADR dependency are known.
